description: A geometry library for engineering drawings and models, in two dimensions and in three. Points, vectors, lines, polylines, polygons, faces with holes, circles and oriented rectangles in the plane; points, planes, triangles, polygons, faces, solids, boxes, coordinate systems and transformations in space. Over both: distance, projection, containment, intersection, collision, parallelism, parametrization, merging, splitting, extending and trimming, offsetting, and boolean operations. It also carries the label placement that arranges drawing labels clear of each other and of blocked regions, and packs boxes such as drawing views onto sheets of paper. Every comparison is tolerance-aware, because coordinates that come out of a BIM model are never exact.
releaseNotes:
NEW IN 12.1.0

      NEW, ellipses in space
      - GeoEllipse3, an elliptical disc in space, with Core.Ellipse3, read as GeoCircle3 is read: its rim and measures,
        points on and off it, every transformation that can be undone, collisions and crossings against everything a
        circle in space is asked about and another ellipse, flattening and meshes. ProjectToPlane on GeoCircle3 and
        GeoEllipse3 gives the shape seen square onto a plane: a circle of radius 300 tilted 60 degrees from the plan is
        an ellipse 300 by 150 in plan. ProjectToEllipse2 and GeoEllipse2.ToEllipse3 carry an ellipse between space and
        the plane.

      NEW, every query from either side
      - DistanceTo, CollidesWith, GetIntersections, TryIntersectWith and GetShortestLineTo answer from both sides of
        every pair that had one side, the same answer bit for bit, a shortest line reversed.
      - GetShortestLineTo(point) on every shape in the plane, and in space wherever the distance was answered.
      - GeoFace2 is measured by its material: DistanceTo against every shape, and face against face.
      - Flat shapes in space say whether and where they meet, and how far apart they are: triangles, polygons and faces
        against each other, planes, rays, bodies and boxes.

      FIXED
      - Circles and arcs in space: a long segment nearly tangent keeps both crossings; two coplanar circles a hair
        outside each other touch; planes nearly one no longer lose crossings far from the origin.
      - A segment or ray lying in a flat shape's plane touches it where it reaches it.
      - A polygon or face is checked against a body's material, holes and openings included.
      - A body in two pieces either side of a plane is not nought from it.
      - Two boxes across skew edges are not touching more than the tolerance apart.
      - A ray dipping from a plane's tolerance band crosses where it reaches the plane, for the body, its prepared form
        and the BVH; a clash bar dipping into a part from the band now enters it.
      - Two triangles give the same answer whichever is asked first, and touch within the tolerance.
      - Clash, simple-polygon and ring sweeps run along the axis with the fewest pairs, and label placement finds its
        neighbours through an index: the same results to the last bit, much faster where the shapes lay along X.

      SOURCE NOTE
      - A bare null or default given as the shape to some GetShortestLineTo and DistanceTo overloads now matches more
        than one and has to be cast. Code already compiled is not affected.

      Details in CHANGELOG.md.

      Earlier releases: https://github.com/nguyenthanguth/GeometryHelper/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
